title: Golden Hour
description: A flat still life, a clay bottle, a cup and an orange on a linen table against a plaster wall, lit through a window you never see. Drag across the room or turn the sun dial and the day moves: the four-pane patch of sun slides across the table at noon and climbs the wall toward evening, shadows stretch and turn violet, then magenta at dawn and deep blue under the moon, and shafts of dusty light hang in the air. It opens at your own local time, or at golden hour after dark.
intent: Light and time as the whole subject: one control, the hour, drives the sun's direction, the window patch, the light colour and the shadow colour together, so the room shows the time of day without a single label beyond the clock.

sources.name: Bruno Simon, folio 2025, DayCycles
sources.what: MIT. The day, dusk, night and dawn light, shadow and fog colours taken as data, and the idea of blending keyed phases around the clock so shadows are coloured rather than grey. A golden keyframe is added between day and dusk.

sources.name: basement.studio, laboratory sun-ray cone
sources.what: No licence, so re-derived: light shafts as one row of noise stretched along the light direction, brighter near the source. Here the noise is read at the point where each air sample's sun ray crosses the window, so the streaks run parallel to the light.

sources.name: Bruno Simon, folio 2019, floor gradient
sources.what: MIT. A bilinear four-corner gradient, used here as the faint sky bounce tinting the ambient light across the frame.

sources.name: Bruno Simon, My Room in 3D
sources.what: No licence, so re-derived: mixing a light into the scene with a per-channel lighten instead of an add, which keeps the sunlit patch painterly and never blows past the paper.
